title: OOM, Low-Memory Kills, and Process Recovery Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies oom, low-memory kills, and process recovery?
options: Reduce the causal memory ownership and make durable operations recover across process termination.
questions.answer: Reduce the causal memory ownership and make durable operations recover across process termination.
questions.explanation: This answer preserves the underlying platform or delivery contract while requiring representative evidence, explicit failure behaviour, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: A low-memory kill always produces a catchable OutOfMemoryError in the app.
questions.explanation: Catching OutOfMemoryError and retrying the same allocation can loop in a compromised low-memory state and hide the underlying unbounded use.

questions.prompt: Why can the OOM allocation stack be misleading?
questions.answer: It shows the allocation that finally failed, while earlier retention or native/graphics growth may have consumed the memory.
questions.explanation: The response identifies the mechanism that makes the decision reliable instead of relying on a convenient proxy.
